title: Reduction commutes with completed pullback
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes and use the Noetherian adic datum $A,I,P_n=A/I^n$, coefficient sheaves $A_W=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_W$ for $W=T,T'$, and reduction tower of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\Proet},A_T))$ be derived $I$-complete in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], and put $K_n=K\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$. Let $L=Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(T'_{\Proet},A_{T'}))$ be the completed pullback of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and write $g_n^*$ for finite-coefficient module pullback as there.

Then $L$ is derived $I$-complete, and for every $n\geq1$ the projection of its defining derived limit to $Lg_n^*K_n$ induces a functorial isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(T'_{\Proet},(P_n)_{T'}))$,
$$\alpha_n:L\otimes^L_{A_{T'}}(P_n)_{T'}\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_n^*K_n.$$
These isomorphisms commute with the quotient transition maps. For $b\geq a\geq1$ they also commute with normalization: extending $\alpha_b$ from $(P_b)_{T'}$ to $(P_a)_{T'}$ and then using the normalization of the pulled-back reduction tower gives $\alpha_a$ after the canonical scalar-extension associativity identification. For $c\geq b\geq a$ these normalizations satisfy the quotient cocycle, and for equal indices the unit identity. All tensor products in the display are over the indicated sheaves of rings; no identification with an ordinary module derived category is asserted.

proof.text: The existing completedPullback_isCompletion identifies the specified output with intrinsic completion of ordinary pullback. Under the joint constant-coefficient Koszul presentation, completion outputs are complete and the unit criterion detects completeness. Transport the completion-unit isomorphism back through the equivalence for every representative of the output.

Apply the finite-arrow invertibility lemma at each n. Prove naturality directly: the scalar homEquiv is natural on both sides, and the limit projection and finite evaluation are natural transformations.

Apply the proved coherence theorem to this family of invertible arrows. It supplies transition compatibility, normalization invertibility and compatibility, quotient cocycle, and the equal-index unit.

blueprint_sketch.proof:
Derived pullback commutes with derived tensor, so its defining tower is the
reduction tower of $Lg^*K$. Apply finite reduction of adic completion to
this object. Its level $n$ is
$Lg^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda P_n\simeq Lg^*(K\otimes^L_\Lambda P_n)=Lg^*K_n$.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $g\colon T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes and
$M\in D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$. The *completed inverse image* is

$$
g^*_{\mathrm{comp}}M=R\varprojlim\bigl(g^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}\operatorname{red}(M)\bigr)
=R\varprojlim_ng^*\bigl(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_T\bigr)
\in D(T'_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E),
$$

in the notation of [det-pbc-complete-derived-completion]. Then:

1. there is a canonical isomorphism
   $g^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}\operatorname{red}(M)\simeq\operatorname{red}(g^*M)$ in
   $D(\operatorname{Tow}(T'))$, natural in $M$, whose level $n$ is
   $g^*(M_n)\simeq(g^*M)_n$; hence $g^*_{\mathrm{comp}}M\simeq\widehat{g^*M}$ is the
   derived completion of $g^*M$;
2. $g^*_{\mathrm{comp}}M$ is derived $\pi_E$-complete, and for every $n$ there is
   an isomorphism $(g^*_{\mathrm{comp}}M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,T'}}
   (\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_{T'}\simeq g^*M_n$, functorial in $M$ and compatible
   with the transition maps;
3. the completion map $\kappa_{g^*M}\colon g^*M\to g^*_{\mathrm{comp}}M$ is an
   isomorphism if and only if $g^*M$ is derived $\pi_E$-complete
   ([def-pe-derived-complete]).

proof.text:
(1) The module pullback $g^*$ is exact ([det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main]) and
strong monoidal, and $g^*\mathcal O_{E,T}=\mathcal O_{E,T'}$ because both rings
are pulled back from the point. Applied termwise to the cone
$\operatorname{red}(M)_n=M\otimes[\mathcal O_{E,T}\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}\mathcal O_{E,T}]$
it gives $g^*M\otimes[\mathcal O_{E,T'}\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}\mathcal O_{E,T'}]=
\operatorname{red}(g^*M)_n$, compatibly with the transitions; this is an
isomorphism of complexes of towers, natural in $M$
([det-pbc-complete-derived-completion], notation 3; [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution]).
Apply $R\varprojlim$.

(2) By (1) and [det-pbc-complete-derived-completion] (6), applied to $g^*M$ on
$T'$, the object $g^*_{\mathrm{comp}}M=\widehat{g^*M}$ is derived complete and its
reductions are those of $g^*M$, which are $g^*M_n$ by (1), compatibly with the
transitions.

(3) By (1), the map is the completion map of $g^*M$, which is an isomorphism
exactly when $g^*M$ is derived complete ([def-pe-derived-complete]).
